title: Sunny and the Distant Music
description: Little Sonny the quokka hears the faintest music drifting through the bush and follows it into a dreamy twilight. A gentle, musical bedtime story for little ones. Part of Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
It was twilight in the bush, and Sunny was sitting very still, watching the sky turn from orange to purple, when he heard it.

Music.

Very faint. Very far away. Coming from somewhere beyond the ridge, beyond the tall trees, from some other place entirely.

He couldn't make out exactly what it was. Sometimes it sounded like a single note held for a very long time. Sometimes like several notes, very soft, drifting.

He sat and listened for a long while.

It came and went with the breeze. Sometimes clear, sometimes almost gone, sometimes just a feeling rather than a sound.

Sunny thought about all the possible worlds that might be sending music through the twilight. All the things that make music — wind in a hollow log, frogs on a distant pond, something being played somewhere far away by someone who loved it very much.

He didn't need to find the source. He didn't need to understand it.

It was enough to sit here and hear it, faint and sweet, floating across the evening air.

The stars began to appear.

The music faded, very slowly, until it was part of the general hush of the bush at night.

Sunny wasn't sure when he stopped hearing it.

He lay back and looked at the stars, carrying the feeling of the music inside him, warm and light.

Goodnight, little Sunny. Goodnight, distant music. Goodnight, beautiful things that drift to us on the evening air.
